title: Kreiskrankenhaus Greiz-Ronneburg hit by cyberattack; emergency room closed, extortion attempt reported
date_note: A system outage was noticed on the evening of 14 November; the district says the attack was identified on 15 November at about 09:00.
summary: The district of Greiz says a cyberattack hit the Kreiskrankenhaus Greiz-Ronneburg, affecting several unnamed systems. The emergency room closed on 15 November and began admitting emergencies again on the evening of 16 November. A district spokesperson called it an extortion attempt, according to Kommunal and Security Affairs citing MDR; the district says patient safety was not at risk. The state criminal police and prosecutors are investigating.
plain: A German district hospital was hit by a cyberattack and its emergency room had to close for about a day. Officials say patients were not put at risk and an extortion attempt was made.
exec: Shows how an attack on a regional hospital can take an emergency room offline and divert patients; check your own downtime and diversion plans.
action: Healthcare operators: test emergency downtime and patient-diversion procedures and offline backups of clinical systems.
impact: Emergency room unavailable from 15 November until the evening of 16 November; emergencies were routed through the Gera dispatch centre. No ransom amount or data theft has been stated.

validation.note: District statement (primary) plus Kommunal, Freie Presse and kma Online (dpa/MDR). Extortion wording is second-hand via Kommunal and Security Affairs; no page states ransomware or data theft. MDR not read directly.

review.note: Compared 15 Nov detection, ER closure, LKA and prosecutors, patient safety, Gera against district statement; extortion and reopening against Kommunal
